facts.f: National museum of Samoa, housed in a former school built by the German colonial administration.
In the Ministry of Education, Sports & Culture compound at Malifa (cnr Ififi/Vaitele Streets), in an over-hundred-year-old colonial building.
Holds Lapita pottery, stone adze heads, historical photographs, information on tattooing and examples of Samoan birds.

apia-3.bio_suggestion: Samoa's national museum in a century-old German school at Malifa, with Lapita pottery, adzes, old photographs and tattoo history.

facts.f: Oldest national park in Samoa, established 1978, 5019 ha on southern-central Upolu from Mount Fito to the coast.
Includes uplands, valleys, marshes, the O Le Pupu lava field and coastal cliffs; designated a Ramsar wetland in 2016.
Trails include a six-hour return walk to Pe'ape'a Cave (lava tube with swiftlets) and the 700 m Ma Tree Walk to a giant buttressed tree.
A 3 km unsealed access road leads to the O Le Pupu lava coast, a rocky coastal trail along lava cliffs.

o-le-pupu-pue-national-park.bio_suggestion: Samoa's oldest national park, running from Mount Fito to a rugged lava coast, with rainforest trails, the Ma Tree and Pe'ape'a Cave.

facts.f: A cenote-like collapse doline in the lava field whose origin is a lava tube that reached the sea; the ceiling fell in about 20 m from the cliff.
Swimming hole about 30 m deep with turquoise water, reached by a long wooden ladder, on the Main South Coast Road.
Half way down the vertical walls is a small platform and wooden ladder to a floating jetty in the water.
Run by a local family; adult fee 20 tala.

to-sua-ocean-trench.bio_suggestion: A 30 m deep seawater swimming hole in a collapsed lava tube near Lotofaga, reached by a long wooden ladder.

facts.f: Lava flows created tubes connecting the clifftop with the ocean; waves force water up through them in fountains.
Also called the Taga Blowholes, on the south-west coast of Savai'i in Palauli district, entered from Taga village, south-west of Salelologa wharf.
Fountains spray every few seconds; the village charges a small admission since land is customary-owned.
Rocks are slippery; guides throw coconuts into the blowholes and then ask for money for photos.

savaii-1.bio_suggestion: Lava-tube blowholes by Taga village where waves shoot fountains from the clifftop rock every few seconds.

facts.f: Customary-owned conservation area on Savai'i's north-west peninsula.
Canopy walk: a 24 m bridge strung between two large trees almost 10 m above the forest floor, then a ladder to a platform in a nearly 230-year-old banyan.
Wikivoyage: a 25 m canopy walkway and a platform in the trees that sleeps six (no toilet).

savaii-6.bio_suggestion: Village-run rainforest preserve on Savai'i's north-west tip, with a 24 m canopy bridge to a platform in a 230-year-old banyan.
